Pocket Flight aircraft realism audit

12 October 2026 · local review · no publication

Verdict: the visible defects are repaired, but the fleet is only partially realistic. All four now use the shared force and rigid-body moment model with component mass, CG and inertia. Physical parameters remain conceptual rather than measured flight-test data. This audit establishes the geometry, rendering and simulator checks described below; it does not establish regulatory compliance or airworthiness.

Current flight dynamics validation

Open the new fleet dynamics validation for the implemented model, aircraft-specific sizing, 32 unassisted trim conditions, browser departures and seeded landings. The geometry evidence below remains the saved before/after asset review.

Checks against the handbook

RequirementEvidenceBoundary
Surface fit, glazing and manufacturing details · §§13.3, 16.1, 16.520 browser views per inspection pass, covering overall, cockpit, both wings and rear for all four aircraft. Peregrine and Aurelia panel joints are checked against the actual upper skin within 1.2 mm. Aurelia cap centres contain closed surface geometry; Peregrine’s bows have a 40 mm flat profile.External fit checks and existing Finch pilot-clearance tests. Complete occupant-envelope and pressure-vessel load analysis have not been performed for the jets.
Independent moving parts and preserved pivots · §§16.2–16.3Exact node hierarchy and authored transforms retained. 16 Aurelia animation clips preserved. Tests exercise periodic control/gear/cockpit programmes, scrubbing and reset across all aircraft.Mechanism motion and finite transforms do not establish full swept-volume collision clearance.
Gear and ground support · §12Fleet tests cover pavement/grass touchdowns, grounded tire clearance, airfield starts and attached contact assemblies. Rendered gear geometry and wheel datums were preserved.No tire load/strain, structural drop-test or emergency braking energy validation.
Propulsion, lighting and layout · §§11, 16.4Inspection covers intake/exhaust views and the published left-red/right-green navigation-light mappings. Aurelia is configured without afterburner. Finch’s propeller thrust is bounded by static thrust and available power.Jet thrust maps and fuel rates are now explicit estimates, with measured-data calibration and inlet pressure recovery unresolved. Structural load paths are inferred from geometry, not analysed.
Weight, stability and handling · §§4, 7–9, 14Finch declares a 860 kg component mass budget, measured wing geometry and force-based lift/drag. Tests cover takeoff, landing, stall, crosswind, density and mass effects, and beginner assist.Jets have no corresponding complete mass/CG/inertia budgets. Their game constants are not physical aircraft specifications. No aircraft has measured aerodynamic polars or demonstrated structural limits.
Private wind-tunnel analysisAll four measured wings solve at 45 m/s, sea-level density and 4° incidence using 48 panels. Wind-tunnel/airflow tests pass; geometry revision hashes were refreshed.Steady incompressible horseshoe-vortex model with a straight fixed wake; main wing only. It does not validate stall, separated flow, compressibility, dynamic stability or full-aircraft CFD.

Verification

  • 59 focused aircraft, handling, gear, aerodynamic and airflow tests passed; 47955 assertions; zero failures.
  • All five new regression checks fail against the preserved original assets and pass against the repairs.
  • All four aircraft load and render in the browser with zero captured errors.
  • 35 private mechanical-showcase browser checks passed; 0 captured errors.
  • Exact asset-preservation checks passed for the three changed GLBs. Unaffected meshes, materials, original buffers, hierarchy and animation clips retained.
  • Main and private tester TypeScript/production builds passed. No deployment was performed.
  • Repaired Peregrine and Aurelia GLBs imported independently into Blender, saved as editable native files, and reopened successfully. Aurelia retains 16 native animation actions.

Code graph and repair workflow

Graph queries traced makeAircraft through game selection, replay and Stormbird’s viewer, and refineAircraftMaterials through the shared loader and private scene. The physics graph led to the force-model distinction verified in current src/physics.ts. Binary geometry conclusions were checked directly against assets, ray intersections, regression tests and rendered views.

  1. After authoring exports: /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender --background --factory-startup --python scripts/repair-airframe-details.py.
  2. Refresh measurements: bun scripts/measure-fleet.ts --save.
  3. Validate: bun scripts/audit-airframe-details.ts and bun test ./tests/airframe-details.test.ts.
  4. Capture matched views with the local inspection server: bun scripts/run-airframe-review.ts after.

The patcher changes only named detail primitives and inverted closed airfoil orientations in the original glTF document. It preserves editable repair code and original assets under output/fleet-detail-before. It is idempotent; -- --rebuild deliberately regenerates these repairs from the retained original assets.

Editable repaired models

Native files: assets/peregrine/Peregrine-HX27-detail-fixed.blend and assets/aurelia/Aurelia-S32-flight-detail-fixed.blend. Both reopen with the required wing, flap, aileron, rudder and landing-gear nodes. Regenerate and validate them with Blender --background --factory-startup --python scripts/save-repaired-aircraft.py.

Engineering references

Project acceptance rules: Principles of Making Planes, especially §§12, 13.1–13.4 and 16.1–16.5. Technical context: FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, construction and controls chapters, and FAA Airplane Flying Handbook, takeoff, landing and jet-operation chapters. These references explain the engineering functions; they do not certify these fictional assets.
